text:
mira: quick check: for the v2 -> v3 streaming cutover i prototyped a \"coexistence operator\" that can route per-tenant to either envelope-shim, frame-shim, or direct passthrough. should we push operator-first or ship per-node sidecars? thinking about upgrade pain and tenant-level control. tagging @jason @kate
jason: operator-first. sidecars are easy to reason about but we end up with many copies and upgrade windows. operator centralizes decision logic and lets us tune per-tenant without redeploys.
kate: operator sounds fine if we can guarantee low added latency and clear diagnostics. we need instant visibility when a tenant flips. also want per-tenant circuit-breakers.
samir: pros/cons: operator = single control plane, easier billing attribution, canary via metadata. cons = new controller code, possible single point of configuration failure. sidecar = isolation but higher infra cost.
mira: my prototype: operator watches a ShimPolicy CRD (reuse routing CRD) and evaluates rules in order: header, tenantLabel, then payload-sample. it patches an annotation on tenant metadata that our ingress uses to route. example policy:
```yaml
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: ShimPolicy
spec:
  match:
    headerContains: \"x-redwood-client: v3\"
    tenantLabels: [\"migrating\", \"trial\"]
  route:
    primary: frame_shim_v3
    fallback: envelope_legacy
  tuning:
    max_in_flight: 64
    enable_batching: true
  safety:
    max_error_pct: 4
    window_seconds: 300
  auditTag: \"shim:frame_v3\"
```
jason: reuse routing CRD, yes. add an explicit `detectionOrder` and `priority` so we don't get ambiguous matches. also ensure operator can shadow traffic to new shim without switching live traffic.
kate: important: detection must handle clients that don't send headers. sniff first frame for a v3 magic token, then route accordingly. and make the debug endpoint human-friendly for support folks.
ops-ux: can we add a console toggle per-tenant and an API for audit logs? ops needs to flip tenants quickly and see change history.
samir: telemetry must include shim_id, shim_latency_p50/p95, shim_errors_total and a baggage tag `shim_route` on spans. without that tracing across operator->shim->runtime will be terrible.
mira: good call. i'll emit shim_route and include a short-lived correlation id. also the operator will annotate billing logs with `auditTag`.
jason: rollout plan: 0.5% shadow -> 1% live -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. gates: increase in p95 > 10% or error_rate > 2% triggers automatic rollback and page.
kate: add a prefix-cache validation smoke test. last migration had a cache thrash problem and we saw p95 spike for 20 minutes.
mira: safety idea: operator keeps a migration state per-tenant: {observing, shadowing, live, rollback}. transitions require passing checks. add manual approval at 10% and 50%.
samir: ops note: operator must expose an emergency kill switch (global) and per-tenant opt-out. we also need an infra-security review for a controller that modifies routing.
infra-bot: infra-bot: security review required for controllers that mutate ingress routing. open ticket in #eng-security with design doc and runbook.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: branch `arch/coexist-operator-v1` created, CI started. unit tests: running.
mira: i'll open an RFC follow-up PR with the ShimPolicy schema, rollout runbook, metrics dashboard templates, and a short playbook for rollbacks. aiming to canary next week.
jason: please include cost delta estimates (operator infra + saved sidecar mem/disk) in the RFC so finance can sign off.
kate: +1 for operator-first if we can validate latency and have good diagnostics.
ops-ux: i'll mock up a console toggle with audit trail; will share a quick prototype tomorrow.
mira: thanks. i'll file the security ticket and draft the runbook. ping me if you want to pair on the smoke tests. :thumbsup:
